brand_notes.materials: 1000D Cordura exterior throughout (400D/420D nylon liner inside), matte woven finish, no laminate sheen. Seams are sewn and bar-tacked at stress points, not welded or taped like Ortlieb's line - visible straight stitch rows, not a smooth weld bead. Nearly every closure uses black-oxide YKK zippers or black plastic YKK/duraflex-style hardware; webbing is black mil-spec nylon.
brand_notes.colorBlocking: Road Runner's identity is deliberate panel color-blocking - solid Cordura colorways (black, burgundy, grey, navy, olive, rust, coyote) are the volume sellers, but the brand also runs multi-panel 'Hybrid' colorways that mix teal/hot-pink/purple/turmeric across distinct front, top and side panels (see anywhere-pannier-4.jpg for a built example: orange bib flap + orange side gusset against a teal body). Where a product's own catalog colorways list includes a two-tone 'main'/'accent' split (most of the Cordura solids do - dark accent trim on a lighter body, or vice versa) or a named multi-color way (Hybrid, The Jaystone, The Clint), that split is carried into this file's colorways array and should render as distinct panels, not one flat color.
brand_notes.mountFamilies: Bar bags (Jammer/Middle Earth/Jumbo Jammer, all four Burritos) mount with two vertical straps over the bars/stem plus a hook-and-loop headtube strap as a third point ('eliminate sway'); none of them use a rack or cage. Stem bags (Auto-Pilot, Co-Pilot, Point N Shooter L) share one three-point system: a permanently-attached vertical stem strap, a removable vertical handlebar strap, and a horizontal headtube strap. Frame bags (Wedge Half/Full) strap to the top tube and down tube (full frame bag adds a third strap parallel to the seat tube) with long hook-and-loop wraps, no bolts. Seat-area bags split into two unrelated mounts: the Sleeper clamps saddle rails AND the seatpost (velcro seatpost strap + rail buckles, like Ortlieb/Apidura seatpacks), while the Drafter and the Tool Saddle Roll attach to the saddle rails ONLY - no seatpost strap on either - and hang free behind the saddle nose. The two Buoys are fork-leg dry bags secured with removable straps (Voile-style, sold separately from the bag itself) along the fork leg. The Anywhere Pannier is the outlier: a rack-only bag with two coral quick-release hook clips at the top plus three Nano-Voile straps threaded through for security, not a QL-style rail.
brand_notes.dimensionPolicy: Every Road Runner product page publishes inches, not cm, and several publish an explicit min-max range. Per the new rule, len/wid use the unfurled (max or fixed) figure and hgt uses the minimum of any height range. This corrected THREE products whose figures in data/brands.json had used the wrong end of a range: Drafter Saddle Bag (was hgt 17.8 cm = the 7in MAX of a published 5.5-7in range; corrected to 14.0 cm = 5.5in MIN - see the Drafter note below), Auto-Pilot Stem Bag (was hgt 21.6 cm = 8.5in; the page gives a 7-8.5in range, corrected to 17.8 cm = 7in MIN), and Sleeper Saddle Bag (was len 33.0 cm, derived by an old 30%-roll-down formula from a 10-20in range; corrected to len 50.8 cm = the 20in UNFURLED max, with the ridden/rolled length carried separately in render.len_cm using the page's own 10in minimum). The Buoy and Micro Buoy fork bags had the same problem in the other direction - both had len set to the ROLLED (short) figure instead of the unrolled max; both corrected, with the rolled figure preserved in render.len_cm. Six products (both Point-N-Shooter/stembag siblings Co-Pilot and PNS-L, Bluff, both Wedge frame bags, and the Anywhere Pannier) publish only a single dimension triple or already had the range's minimum correctly selected, so those needed no change.
brand_notes.drafterFinding: The Drafter Saddle Bag is confirmed to have been drawing 3.8 cm too tall: data/brands.json and the prior model pass used dims_cm.hgt = 17.8 cm, which is 7in - the MAXIMUM of the maker's published 5.5in-7in height range, not the minimum the new rule requires. Corrected hgt is 14.0 cm (5.5in). Separately, and just as important for the seat-tube collision: the Drafter is rail-only. The maker page (roadrunnerbags.us/products/drafter-saddle-bag) says explicitly to 'loop the webbing through the rails of your saddle and under the front strap' and that the bag 'rolls toward the back of the saddle' - there is no seatpost strap at all, confirmed visually in drafter-1.jpg and drafter-3.jpg (both show the bag hanging entirely from a rail loop with a single front buckle, never touching the seatpost). This file's mount block sets attachesTo to saddle_rails only. If the renderer was also treating this bag like a seatpost-clamped seatpack (pulling its nose down onto the seatpost/seat-tube axis the way the Sleeper or an Ortlieb Seat-Pack does), that would independently push its body toward the seat tube regardless of height. Fixing the height closes most of the 5.1mm gap by itself (3.8cm >> 5.1mm); if any residual intrusion remains after that, I'd look next at whether the mount code is still pulling this bag toward attachesTo:['seatpost'] instead of respecting a rail-only mount.
